note: The ticks on each card: checks of the catalogue's entry in catalogues.yaml, evaluated without network access. See docs/README.md, section "3. Availability probe".

fields.passes: The entry has all seven required fields: id, node, name, type, protocol, endpoint and source.
fields.why: Every card, filter and probe relies on these fields.
fields.caveat: Always green on the page: a file with a missing field is rejected by config.load() before the page is built.

node.passes: The node id is one of the 16 known EOSC Nodes, the same ids as in eosc-basic-compliance.
node.why: The card can show the node's name, colour and logo, and results can be joined with the landing-page checks by node.

protocol.passes: A Service Catalogue is queried through the EOSC EU Node services API (een-services-api); a Research Product Catalogue through OAI-PMH (oai-pmh).
protocol.why: The probe picks its request from the protocol, so a mismatch would query the catalogue the wrong way.

https.passes: The endpoint queried starts with https://.
https.why: Catalogues are queried over encrypted connections only.

oai-base.passes: Research Product Catalogues only: the endpoint is the OAI-PMH base URL, with no request such as ?verb=Identify attached.
oai-base.why: The probe adds ?verb=Identify itself; a copied request URL would produce a broken query.

source:production.passes: source is production: the endpoint was taken from the production sheet (production_env_node_services.xlsx).
source:production.why: Keeps the provenance of every endpoint explicit.

source:resource-hub.passes: source is resource-hub: the note names the Hub record (a 21.11166/… PID), and nothing is quoted from the sheet.
source:resource-hub.why: The production sheet does not list this catalogue; naming the Hub record keeps it traceable, and the Hub has no comment column to quote.
